answer: Newcomers begin as a diffuse nebula: a cloud of tiny verified acts, each one re-run by a random established peer before it counts. A tide of surprise audits sweeps the cloud at unpredictable intervals, re-checking one random act live; acts that fail dissolve, and the identity's stake erodes with them. Only clouds that survive many tides condense into a trusted star. Every act is recorded in a public ocean anyone can dive into and inspect, so a fake identity must fake an entire sea of consistent work — far costlier than one real job.
